eye.because: Four clear steps, read from houses A, B and D. Z: B is a plain dwelling (two ground-floor windows with window boxes, door with awning), D is boarded up. Y: B's ground floor has become a shop (blank panel under a fascia, window gone, dark patch on the front above), D still boarded. W: B has gained a glazed veranda with a balcony on its side, and D's windows are open again. X: same as W, but A's big plate-glass shopfront has gone and been replaced by ordinary windows with a new extra window. I took growth and additions to run forward (house, then shop, then extension, then A's shop closing). That direction is my judgement; the reverse would need an extension demolished and a shop turned back into a house, which seems less likely. The years are guesses from style (shopfronts, veranda, mansard roof, so roughly early to mid 20th century).

street.because: Visible changes are on D, E and C only. W and Z: D's gable windows are boarded and E's windows are open. X and Y: D's window is open and E's are boarded, so I read D reoccupied and E left empty, which puts them later. Y alone has C's windows fitted with casings and sills, which I read as the last addition. W and Z look identical to me, so their order is a coin flip. The years are guesses.

12m.because: W and X: D's three windows are boarded (crossed boards) and E's windows are open. Z and Y: D's windows are open and E's are boarded. Y alone has casings and sills on C's windows, so I put it last. W and X look identical to me, so their order is a coin flip. The years are guesses.

city.because: Read from A and B, matching the eye view. X: B has ground-floor windows and a window box, and A has its shopfront. W: B's ground floor is now a blank shop panel, A still has its shopfront. Y: B has the side veranda and balcony, and A still has its shopfront. Z: B has the veranda, and A's shopfront has been replaced by separate windows. The sequence matches the eye view's B and A changes. The years are guesses.
